Therefore, the leading coefficient of f(x)g(x) is relatively prime to the least common multiple of the denominators of the leading coefficients of f(x)g(x). This implies that f(x)g(x) is primitive.

Let p(x) be the least common multiple of the denominators of the leading coefficients of f(x) and g(x). Since f(x) and g(x) are coprime, their leading coefficients are relatively prime to p(x). Therefore, there exist polynomials a(x) and b(x) in R[x] such that a(x)p(x) + b(x)p(x) = 1.
